A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing additions and removals to be distinguished from relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-injection experiments, causal interventions on model components, feature analyses, and learned-vector training results.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds preference-training experiments, cross-model refusal-ablation tests, geometric controls, and downstream evaluations.

M1.justification: The learned steering vector, renamed a bias vector, retains its training procedure. v4 adds a procedural variant for cross-model refusal ablation: a uniform per-model projection weight selected by a minimum-effective-dose rule (Appendix C.2), alongside the original approach using optimized regional weights.

E1.justification: v4 adds preference training using Dolci-Instruct-DPO and downstream evaluation on HaluEval, JailbreakHub, MMLU/GPQA-based chain-of-thought faithfulness tasks, and 1,900 self-written-versus-prefilled response examples. These substantially extend the represented data and task requirements beyond v1's concept-injection and generic-prompt evaluations.

E2.justification: v4 introduces comparisons among standard, reference-free, shuffled, and reversed DPO; chosen/rejected-response SFT; SFT with KL; margin-plus-KL training; and DPO without prior SFT (Table 3). Cross-model refusal experiments also add magnitude-matched random-direction controls. These are evaluated comparators absent from v1.

E3.justification: v1 aggregates OLMo results over layers 25, 32, 38, 45, and 51; v4 reports layer-specific evaluations at 19, 22, and 25 on 50 concepts. New experiments introduce controlled LoRA training, TPR-minus-FPR comparisons, and logit-based refusal-ablation evaluation. The attention-probe target also changes in the prose from steered/unsteered activations to successful/failed concepts, although v4 Figure 27 retains the old caption.

E4.justification: v4 adds training-objective and data-domain ablations, DPO beta sweeps, norm/unembedding controls, binary-classification analysis, trial-number sensitivity findings, and cross-model refusal controls. It also investigates downstream side effects. Conversely, the PLS2 steering analysis and v1 Figure 14b-d's circuit-importance analyses disappear; Figure 14a is retained as v4 Figure 33.

E5.justification: v4 newly specifies the existing 100 injection trials as 10 trial numbers with 10 samples each and discusses sampling and judge variability (Appendix B.3); this does not establish additional runs. Appendix H adds correlations controlling for other vector properties. Existing confidence-interval and cross-validation reporting largely persists, without new training-seed information.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include TPR-minus-FPR of +14.4 percentage points for standard DPO versus -13.5 for chosen-response SFT (Table 3). Newly reported downstream comparisons show MMLU faithfulness falling from 37.5% to 21.5% and prefill detection from 36.3% to 16.1% with the bias vector. These are new evaluations; the retained concept-injection gains are unchanged. OLMo results are replaced under revised settings.

T1.justification: The auxiliary circuit-importance definition, gate attribution multiplied by steering projection, is removed with the corresponding analysis. The central steering-attribution mathematics, including complete-cut conditions and Equations 1-3, remains unchanged between v1 Appendix M and v4 Appendix Q.

C1.justification: The central post-training claim becomes more specific: v4 attributes emergence to contrastive preference optimization, with standard SFT insufficient, rather than broadly to post-training. This algorithm-level conclusion enters the abstract, introduction, and discussion. The main claims about behavioral robustness, distributed detection mechanisms, and underelicited capacity are retained.

C2.justification: Appendix S substantially narrows the interpretation of learned-vector improvements: they do not transfer to broader self-knowledge, and shorter, more assertive responses accompany degraded faithfulness and prefill detection. v4 also qualifies zero-FPR findings to trial numbers 1-10, reports confabulation outside that range, and explicitly acknowledges that the mechanism of post-training emergence remains unidentified.

D1.justification: v4 supplies detailed LoRA hyperparameters, optimizer and schedule settings, preference-data access information, and an abliterated-model link. It clarifies model-matched concept vectors, shared transcoder usage, intervention token positions, and logit-based estimators. Some information is lost: v1's explicit refusal-ablation region boundaries and optimization search bounds are omitted.

R1.justification: v4 adds substantive comparisons with Pearson-Vogel et al., Lederman and Mahowald, and Rivera and Africa, relating cached-representation detection, probability matching, latent capacity, and trained steering awareness to its findings. Benchmark and faithfulness references also expand. This materially broadens the research positioning beyond v1's discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, mechanistic explanations, and discussion receive extensive editing. Section 4 is reframed, Section 6 distinguishes the learned bias from injected concept vectors, related work is reorganized, and limitations become a separate section before discussion. The appendices are substantially reorganized, beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned, gate panels from v1 Figures 10-12 are consolidated into v4 Figure 11, and positive-attribution displays are regrouped in Appendix L. The circuit-distribution panel moves to Appendix O while other circuit-importance panels disappear. Layer-specific OLMo plots, new diagnostic figures, and multiple experimental tables substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly associated introspection with checkpoint stage and assessed broader learned-vector effects through response style and length. v4 adds controlled training comparisons that substantially strengthen the preference-training explanation, and downstream tests expose important limits and adverse effects previously untested. Geometric controls further strengthen the mechanistic evidence. These gains outweigh the removal of some circuit-importance evidence and reporting inconsistencies, including Table 9's caption conflicting with the domain-sufficiency interpretation in Section 3.3.
